domain: Communications, networking, cryptography and constellation operations

bottlenecks.name: Spectrum sharing and interference compliance
bottlenecks.description: More than 10,000 commercial communications satellites operate in LEO with 50,000+ more planned (Roberts, arXiv 2609.36122). Each new system has to show that it does not degrade GSO networks, earlier NGSO systems, terrestrial users or radio astronomy beyond set limits. In 2026 the FCC moved from fixed EPFD power masks to performance-based criteria: no more than 3% time-weighted throughput degradation and 0.4% (NGSO-NGSO) or 0.1% (proposed NGSO-GSO) added unavailability, judged over an orbital simulation (FCC 24-117; FCC vote of Apr 30 2026 per 33FG). ITU Article 22 EPFD limits still apply internationally. Direct-to-device adds out-of-band and harmonic problems: the 2620 MHz D2D downlink's second harmonic already causes at least 59% geodetic-VLBI data loss (arXiv 2608.11659).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Mostly expert-scarce rather than open. Needed: certified (interval or proof-backed) bounds on aggregate interference and time-percentage statistics instead of Monte Carlo tails; beam-cell assignment under interference budgets (NP-hard in general, provably near-optimal in special cases, e.g. SkyShare arXiv 2609.00821); game-theoretic coexistence with convergence and uniqueness proofs (arXiv 2609.38935). Genuinely open: tight guarantees for coexistence among three or more equal-priority operators. No catalog family applies; the unlock is capability (P1) plus certified numerics (P2).

bottlenecks.name: Mesh routing, topology and radio resource management at 10,000+ satellites
bottlenecks.description: Laser inter-satellite meshes with 3-4 terminals per satellite, topology that changes continuously, and user-beam handovers about every 15 s (Roberts). The joint problem of pairing laser terminals, routing traffic and allocating rates is NP-hard per topology snapshot (arXiv 2601.21914). Academic designs report 35-145% throughput gains over non-joint baselines and up to 2.3x capacity over +Grid on real Starlink data (arXiv 2602.07756), but operator practice is proprietary and the baselines are naive.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Expert-scarce. Because exact optimality is NP-hard, the useful product is a certificate: a dual bound that says how far the running solution is from optimal, plus decompositions with proven convergence. Agents can also write machine-checked proofs that routing and handover logic is loop-free and converges under churn (P2). Catalog ties are ceilings (102 UGC, T3; 117 sparsest-cut hardness, T1) and a matching speedup (120, T1) that does not matter at this scale.

bottlenecks.name: Tasking, scheduling and ground segment
bottlenecks.description: Earth-observation tasking, downlink and ground-station-as-a-service scheduling, ground-station siting, and optical-ground-station weather diversity. Benchmarks now reach 1,000 satellites and 10,000 requests (EOS-Bench, arXiv 2604.25782); exact integer programming for ground-station selection stops scaling before a ~100-satellite fleet (arXiv 2510.03438). For optical ground networks the bottleneck has moved from peak rate to repeatable service under weather, acquisition and scheduling constraints (Turyshev, arXiv 2606.23711).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Expert-scarce, with ceilings newly proven. Teams need bespoke formulations of each mission's constraints, exact solvers on structured instances and certified-gap heuristics. The catalog adds hardness ceilings (102 T3; 117 and 125 headlines T1), an exact three-machine precedence scheduler (124, T1) and online guarantees (110, 111, T1). These act through P3 within months; most value is P1.

bottlenecks.name: Physical layer: optical links, channel coding and direct-to-device link budgets
bottlenecks.description: Optical links are now proven at 200 Gbps from LEO (TBIRD), 1.8 Gbps operational GEO relay (EDRS) and 267 Mbps from about 19 million miles (DSOC, ended Sep 2 2025). Deep-space optical links are photon-starved and use PPM with superconducting single-photon detectors. Direct-to-device links close with handset antennas and depend on spectrum, aperture and power (Starlink's +10 dB waiver, Mar 2025). Coding is near capacity for long blocks; short packets (D2D signaling, IoT, telecommand) still lose fractions of a dB to finite-blocklength limits.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Mixed. Long-block coding is solved; short-block code and decoder design is expert-scarce, and LLM-guided search already finds record codes (arXiv 2609.37056). Receivers that beat photon counting (joint detection approaching the Holevo limit) are genuinely open physics-engineering theory. Catalog: 273 (entropy photon-number inequality, T1) proves multi-user optical capacity limits, a confidence result that changes no hardware.

bottlenecks.name: Security: post-quantum migration, crypto-agility and cryptanalysis risk
bottlenecks.description: Satellites live 15 years in GEO; NIST IR 8547 (draft, Nov 2024) deprecates 112-bit RSA/ECC by 2030 and disallows all quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms by 2035. Post-quantum authentication is expensive on constrained, high-latency links (arXiv 2607.23007). Resource estimates for breaking RSA-2048 fell to under a million noisy qubits (Gidney, May 2025). AI cryptanalysis is real but so far hits only non-standard constructions (arXiv 2608.21986).
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Implementation and protocol verification is expert-scarce: machine-checked correctness, constant-time and masking proofs for PQC on space processors, and proofs of key-management and in-orbit update protocols (P2). Lattice hardness itself is a genuinely open question; nothing in the release touches it (tl-position-5), and 279 and 138 are not attacks. The capability pointed at cryptanalysis is the watch item.

bottlenecks.name: Quantum communications from space
bottlenecks.description: Satellite QKD is moving from Micius-class demos to small payloads and portable ground stations: Jinan-1's 23 kg payload delivered up to 1.07 Mbit of secure key per pass and a China-South Africa key over 12,900 km (Nature, Mar 2025). Eagle-1 launches late 2026/early 2027 for three years of validation (ESA). Short passes make finite-key effects and device imperfections the limiting theory problem; loss, background light and weather the limiting physics.
bottlenecks.ondemand_math_help: Finite-key security proofs that include real device flaws and non-IID signals are partly open and highly specialized (arXiv 2606.29943, 2605.12984), so on-demand help plus formalization (Lean-QIT, arXiv 2607.09632) is the unlock. Catalog: 276 (T3), 266 and 272 (T1) settle ceilings and change no flown protocol.

nodes.title: AI agents audit cryptography at research grade
nodes.description: Frontier models run closed-loop cryptanalysis: they propose attacks on published schemes, protocols and parameter sets, test them, and return exact witnesses for a human to judge. Achieved here means standards bodies and major vendors routinely run such audits on candidate schemes and parameters.
nodes.status_oct2026: Partly exists. Olejnik and Naskręcki (arXiv 2608.21986, Aug 22 2026) report an autonomous agent workflow that found failures in eight published constructions, for example a Ring-LWR commitment that opens to any message and a lattice e-voting protocol that loses receipt-freeness. None is a NIST-standardized scheme. ML attacks on LWE recover only sparse or small secrets at reduced parameters (NoMod, arXiv 2510.02162). openai/math contains no attack on factoring, discrete log or lattices (tl-position-5).
nodes.why: The failures found so far sit one level above the hardness assumption: encodings, simulators, parameter certification, protocol composition. That is where space security is weakest. Bespoke key-management and command-authentication protocols on constrained links are written by small teams and rarely reviewed by cryptographers. Once research-grade models are public (cap-research-math-public), an audit that took a specialist weeks costs hours of compute, so every new satellite security protocol can be attacked before launch. Under S2 agent task horizons double every 6-9 months, so by 2028 agents audit whole protocol suites, not single constructions.
nodes.strongest_case_small: The breaks so far are in obscure, non-standard constructions. Standardized primitives (AES-256, ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA) have decades of expert scrutiny. Most real-world failures come from implementation bugs and key handling, which human audits with existing tools already target.
nodes.signpost: An AI-found break or parameter downgrade in an IETF, CCSDS or NIST-standardized scheme; NIST or CCSDS stating that AI audits were used in a selection or review.

nodes.title: AI finds a structural weakness in post-quantum lattices
nodes.description: Watch item, not a forecast: an AI-produced, independently verified result that cuts the concrete security of ML-KEM or ML-DSA parameter sets by 10 or more bits, or gives a subexponential algorithm for module-lattice problems. If it happens, satellites with lattice-only key exchange need an in-orbit algorithm swap.
nodes.status_oct2026: Nothing in openai/math touches lattices, LWE, isogenies or discrete log (tl-position-5). Family 138 (Subset Sum in 2^0.49n worst case, T1) and 279 (exact quantum factoring, T1) are not attacks. Outside the release, a single-author, multi-part arXiv claim of a polynomial-time quantum attack on Module-LWE over 2-power cyclotomics (Luo, arXiv 2605.17412, May 2026) is unrefereed, and we found no expert endorsement. A similar 2024 quantum-lattice claim was withdrawn after a bug was found (general).
nodes.why: Whether module lattices are hard is a fact about mathematics. AI capability cannot make them weak, only find a weakness that already exists. But the capability that produced the release's theoretical-CS results in weeks raises the chance that hidden structure, if it exists, is found inside the horizon; 2-power cyclotomic rings are the most-suspected surface. Chain: weakness found -> NIST revises or deprecates parameters -> satellites with lattice-only key exchange and no update path are exposed for the rest of a 15-year life. The hedge already exists: HQC (code-based, selected Mar 11 2025, final standard expected 2027) and hash-based signatures. Bands are judgments about discovery, not computed probabilities.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Lattice problems have resisted about 30 years of cryptanalysis and come with worst-case to average-case reductions. ML-KEM-1024 has a large margin: even a 10-bit loss leaves it far outside attack range. The base rate of a practical break by 2031 is very low regardless of AI.
nodes.signpost: Any lab release containing LWE, SIS or NTRU results; a Comparator-checked Lean proof of an improved lattice-reduction bound; a NIST statement re-examining ML-KEM parameters; the outcome of expert review of arXiv 2605.17412.

nodes.title: Proven ceilings for scheduling and network partitioning
nodes.description: Approximation limits that planners assumed become theorems. Beating the Goemans-Williamson Max-Cut ratio or a factor-2 vertex cover is NP-hard (UGC). Uniform sparsest cut has no constant-factor algorithm. Metric k-median siting is pinned at 1+2/e. Companion results: polynomial-time three-machine precedence scheduling and optimal-order randomized k-server.
nodes.status_oct2026: 102 Unique Games [L], T3: Lean covers the UGC theorem and the vertex-cover factor below two. 117: the Lean main result is the semidefinite integrality gap (OAI.UniformSparsestCut.mainGap); the NP-hardness headline is T1 (statement gap). 125: Lean covers a companion recovery result (KMedianRecovery); the (1+2/e+ε) algorithm headline is T1 pending audit, and the matching hardness bound was already known (general). 124, 110 and 111 are T1. No outside Comparator run reported as of Oct 7 2026; the repo is a single-commit snapshot.
nodes.why: Constellation operations are full of problems with these shapes. Splitting co-channel beams into two frequency groups to minimize conflicts is a Max-Cut variant. Picking a minimal set of links or beams that covers all conflicts is vertex-cover-like. Partitioning a laser mesh to isolate failures or traffic domains is a sparsest-cut problem. Picking gateway or ground-station sites from candidates is k-median. A proven ceiling tells a team to stop funding general-purpose 'optimal' solvers and invest in instance structure and exact methods for small cases (tl-position-3). It also lets buyers discount vendor claims of optimal scheduling at scale. In every scenario this lands within months of independent checking, because the only thing needed is that practitioners hear about it.
nodes.strongest_case_small: These limits were already widely believed, so practice changes little (tl-position-3). Real instances are structured. A 96-satellite ground-station selection or a 10,000-request tasking day is solved well by MIP plus heuristics, and worst-case hardness says nothing about such instances.
nodes.signpost: First independent Comparator run and statement audit on UniqueGamesTheorem.json; a survey or textbook treating UGC as a theorem; mission-planning vendors citing proven ceilings in benchmarks.

nodes.title: Optical multi-user capacity limits become theorems (conditional)
nodes.description: Family 273 claims a proof of the entropy photon-number inequality for beam-splitter mixing of bosonic inputs. This inequality was the missing step for the capacity region of the optical broadcast channel and for the secret-key capacity of optical wiretap channels with thermal noise (general). If the proof holds, the rate limits for one optical transmitter serving several receivers, and for links with an eavesdropper and background light, are proven rather than conjectured.
nodes.status_oct2026: 273 is T1: manuscript only, and not in the repo's list of formalized main results. Single-user capacity of thermal-noise bosonic channels was already proven in 2014 (general). Lean infrastructure for quantum Shannon theory is forming: Lean-QIT formalizes the Holevo-Schumacher-Westmoreland classical-capacity theorem (arXiv 2607.09632, Jul 2026).
nodes.why: Conditional. Engineers sizing optical relays (one GEO or LEO terminal serving several ground stations or users) and analyzing physical-layer secrecy of optical links already use the conjectured formulas; the proof removes the asterisk. The pathway is model confidence (tl-position-2): no link budget or hardware changes. The only difference between S1 and S2 is how fast a T1 quantum-information manuscript reaches T2-T4. In S2, Lean coverage of quantum entropy (building on Lean-QIT) lets an agent formalize it during 2027.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Deployed and planned optical links use direct detection with PPM or on-off keying, well below the Holevo limit, so the gap to capacity is a receiver problem, not a theory problem. Operators use optical terminals point-to-point, not as multi-user broadcasters.
nodes.signpost: A named quantum-optics information theorist endorsing the 273 argument, or a Lean formalization of it built on Lean-QIT.

nodes.title: Settled limits for quantum links
nodes.description: Three quantum-information results bound what space quantum links can do. 276 gives the exact classical capacity of every qubit generalized amplitude-damping channel (loss with thermal noise). 266 shows there are exactly three mutually unbiased bases in dimension six. 272 builds an entangled state with zero distillable secret key and disproves the PPT-squared conjecture.
nodes.status_oct2026: 276 [L], T3 (Lean OAI.GAD.main, Comparator challenge AmplitudeDamping.json; unchecked by outsiders). 266 T1: the exclusion of a fourth basis is a certified binary64 computation. 272 T1.
nodes.why: For space quantum networks, 272 (conditional) says entanglement on a link is not enough to certify key: security must be shown through key-rate proofs, not entanglement witnesses. Because a PPT channel can have a non-entanglement-breaking square, a two-hop relay through such noisy links is not automatically useless. 266 (conditional) confirms that high-dimensional QKD should use prime-power dimensions, which is already practice. 276 gives an exact benchmark for thermal-noise qubit channels such as quantum memories and noisy downlinks. All three are ceilings or confidence results, so they take effect as soon as people read them.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Every planned satellite QKD mission (Eagle-1, SpeQtre, QEYSSat, SPOQC, Jinan-1 successors) runs two-dimensional BB84 or BBM92 or continuous-variable QKD. None of these results changes a protocol, a key rate or a payload.
nodes.signpost: An outside Comparator run on AmplitudeDamping.json; endorsement of 272 by a quantum Shannon theorist, since it disproves a named conjecture.

nodes.title: Explicit optimal expanders (conditional)
nodes.description: 178 builds nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs, the best possible spectral expanders, deterministically for every degree d≥3 and all large even sizes. 177 constructs bounded-degree coboundary expanders in every dimension: the high-dimensional expansion behind locally testable codes and good quantum LDPC codes.
nodes.status_oct2026: Both T1 (manuscript only).
nodes.why: Conditional. A laser mesh in which each satellite has 3-4 terminals is a bounded-degree graph, and Ramanujan graphs give the largest spectral gap at that degree: short paths, high bisection bandwidth and graceful degradation when links fail. Explicit high-dimensional expanders feed code constructions (classical expander codes; qLDPC codes for quantum memories and repeaters). The pathway is new theory into tools (P6), so engineering use inside 2031 is a stretch; the band here is for the mathematics being established.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Random d-regular graphs are already within ε of Ramanujan with high probability, and bipartite Ramanujan graphs of every degree have been known to exist since 2013 (general). Real laser topologies are dictated by orbital geometry, link range, pointing and terminal slew time (+Grid, Motif, demand-aware designs), not by abstract graph choice.
nodes.signpost: A constellation-topology study that imposes Ramanujan-like structure under real geometric constraints and beats the best geometric heuristic by 10% or more in diameter or bisection bandwidth.

nodes.title: Provable interference compliance for shared spectrum
nodes.description: Interference showings for NGSO-GSO and NGSO-NGSO sharing delivered as certified bounds instead of Monte Carlo runs: interval or proof-backed bounds on time-weighted throughput degradation, unavailability and aggregate EPFD, with the model assumptions written as a checkable specification. Achieved means operators use such bounds in at least one filing or bilateral coordination agreement.
nodes.status_oct2026: On Apr 30 2026 the FCC voted to replace its 26-year-old NGSO-GSO EPFD framework with performance-based rules. A Jan 9 2026 waiver (DA 26-36) had already raised co-frequency beams per location from 1 to 8, and GSO-arc avoidance tightened from 4 to 3 degrees (33FG). FCC NGSO-NGSO rules (FCC 24-117) cap time-weighted throughput degradation at 3% and added unavailability at 0.4% over an orbital simulation; the NGSO-GSO proposal used 3% and 0.1% (Roberts, arXiv 2609.36122). ITU Article 22 EPFD limits still govern internationally. Measured low-frequency EPFD from constellations exceeds radio-astronomy thresholds in 50-70% of samples (arXiv 2609.01995). No catalog family applies.
nodes.why: The regulatory shift turned compliance from checking a power mask into a statistical claim about simulating tens of thousands of satellites. Disputes are now about simulation assumptions and tail events. Aggregates are where Monte Carlo is least trustworthy: keeping one interferer under threshold needs 8.1 degrees of separation, five need 15.5 and twenty need 27.0 (Roberts). A certified bound with a written specification can be re-checked by a rival operator or the FCC in hours. The math (geometry, order statistics, interval arithmetic) is expert-scarce rather than open. In S2, research-grade applied math is routine by 2027-28, so the first certified showings appear in 2028; in S1 they wait for public models and some years of diffusion.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Spectrum disputes are commercial and political, not mathematical, and regulators accept Monte Carlo. Certified worst-case bounds are conservative and could cost capacity against statistical showings. The contested inputs (antenna patterns, traffic models, deployment plans) stay contested.
nodes.signpost: An FCC or ITU-R WP4A filing citing machine-checked or interval-certified interference bounds; an operator publishing an open, verified EPFD or degradation calculator.

nodes.title: Near-optimal mesh routing with a proven gap
nodes.description: Per-snapshot joint optimization of laser-terminal pairing, routing, rate allocation and beam/frequency assignment at 10,000+ satellites, solved in seconds with a certified optimality gap (for example a Lagrangian dual bound), so operators know how much capacity the software leaves on the table.
nodes.status_oct2026: The per-snapshot joint problem is NP-hard. A Lagrangian decomposition into matching, shortest paths and an LP gains 35-145% throughput over non-joint baselines in simulation (arXiv 2601.21914), and a graph neural network that predicts the dual prices matches it orders of magnitude faster (arXiv 2601.21921). Topology designs tested on three months of Starlink data report up to 2.3x capacity and 45% lower delay than +Grid (arXiv 2602.07756). The baselines are naive and operator practice is proprietary. Family 120 (almost-linear exact matching and prescribed-degree factors, T1) solves the terminal-pairing subproblem asymptotically fast.
nodes.premise_tier: n/a (capability); T3 for the 102 ceiling, T1 for 117 hardness and 120
nodes.why: A certificate turns a capacity question into an investment decision. With a 3% dual gap, more capacity has to come from terminals, satellites or spectrum; with a 30% gap it can come from software. The math (decompositions, convergence and gap proofs, problem-specific relaxations) is bespoke and easier than the catalog's problems (tl-position-4), so it becomes a P1 item as soon as research-grade models are public. The ceilings (UGC; 117, conditional) say that certified gaps must be instance-specific rather than worst-case.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Operators such as SpaceX already run strong in-house optimization. Realistic gain over their practice is probably 5-20% capacity (judgment), while V3 hardware is a 10x per-satellite step (33FG). Family 120 adds nothing practical at this scale: a 10,000-node, ~50,000-edge matching takes milliseconds with classical algorithms. Terminal count, acquisition time and gateway capacity bind first.
nodes.signpost: An operator, SDA or a vendor publishing optimality-gap metrics for live routing; an open solver with certified gaps at Starlink scale.

nodes.title: Formally verified constellation control plane
nodes.description: Machine-checked proofs that routing, handover and topology-reconfiguration code is loop-free and deadlock-free, converges under link churn and meets latency bounds. Agents produce the proofs and maintain them as the code changes.
nodes.status_oct2026: An agent extended a 3,000-line SMT network verifier with OSPF areas, BGP route reflection and L3VPN by counterexample-guided learning against emulated routers (arXiv 2608.11340, Aug 2026). Satellite-specific work is small, for example model checking of a TDM inter-satellite-link algorithm (arXiv 2511.09485). The broader evidence is the openai/math pipeline: 127 families with agent-written Lean (T3), strongest in discrete mathematics, which is what protocols need.
nodes.why: With handovers about every 15 s and a continuously changing topology, test coverage of control-plane states is poor; proofs cover all states. Commercial communications networks face no certification gate, so progress is limited by writing specifications of dynamic topologies, which agents began doing in 2026. Discrete properties formalize well: 20 of 40 theoretical-CS families in the release have Lean proofs.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Mega-constellation operators ship software weekly and value iteration speed over proofs. Outages come more from hardware faults, space weather and the ground segment than from routing logic, and orbital dynamics and timing are hard to specify.
nodes.signpost: An operator or SDA prime disclosing machine-checked proofs for routing or handover code; a satellite-network verifier released by a lab or vendor.

nodes.title: Proven-correct post-quantum crypto for space processors
nodes.description: Agents produce implementations of ML-KEM, ML-DSA, HQC and hash-based signatures for radiation-tolerant processors and FPGAs. Each comes with machine-checked functional correctness, constant-time and masking (side-channel) proofs, plus certified failure-probability bounds.
nodes.status_oct2026: Exists for mainstream CPUs, not yet for space hardware. The Jasmin compiler is proven to preserve the IND-CCA security of an ML-KEM implementation used in Signal (Rocq, arXiv 2511.11292). Lean 4 proofs of arithmetic masking for NTT hardware found that one open accelerator masks only one round (arXiv 2604.20793). A certified ML-KEM-768 decryption-failure bound of 2^-164.81 holds in a stated abstraction (arXiv 2609.09983). NIST picked HQC as its backup KEM on Mar 11 2025; final standard expected 2027.
nodes.why: Most real cryptographic failures are implementation bugs and side channels, not broken mathematics (general). Space adds unusual targets (LEON or radiation-hardened RISC-V cores, FPGAs) and tight memory, so verified libraries must be re-targeted and re-proven. That is proof labor, which agents now supply. Achieved here means a verified library for a space-grade target exists and a flight program uses it; certification credit is a separate node.
nodes.strongest_case_small: FIPS 140-3 and NSA evaluations are test-based and slow. Many satellites use certified hardware crypto modules where code proofs add little, and programs freeze crypto choices years before launch.
nodes.signpost: A verified ML-KEM, ML-DSA or LMS library released for a radiation-hardened processor; a flight program citing machine-checked crypto proofs.

nodes.title: Custom channel codes on request
nodes.description: AI designs codes and decoders for specific links, with machine-checked finite-blocklength performance claims. Targets: short packets for direct-to-device signaling, IoT and telecommand; photon-counting optical links; synchronization and deletion channels.
nodes.status_oct2026: LLM-guided search found seven record binary linear codes, improving 22 table entries, each verified exhaustively (arXiv 2609.37056, Sep 2026). A search for quantum LDPC bivariate-bicycle codes cost about $400 of inference (arXiv 2606.02418). AI-assisted, Lean-formalized information-theory results appeared in Sep 2026: a deletion-channel capacity upper bound (arXiv 2609.13351) and three binary-channel conjectures (arXiv 2609.27991). Short-block polar and LDPC designs sit fractions of a dB from finite-blocklength bounds (arXiv 2503.02782, 2512.17834).
nodes.why: Long-block codes are near capacity, so the remaining gains are in short blocks and unusual channels, where design is expert-scarce rather than open. 0.5 dB is about 12% power, and on a handset uplink at the edge of a beam that can decide whether a link closes. Adoption runs through 3GPP and CCSDS standards cycles of 2-4 years, which binds even in S3.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Coding gains are small next to antenna gain, power and spectrum. Standards bodies are conservative, decoder complexity, latency and patents decide adoption, and most space links already use standardized LDPC, turbo or polar codes.
nodes.signpost: A 3GPP NTN or CCSDS contribution containing an AI-designed code; AI-found record codes appearing in a product.

nodes.title: Tight, machine-checked security proofs for satellite QKD
nodes.description: Composable finite-key security proofs for satellite QKD passes (decoy-state BB84, BBM92, continuous-variable QKD) that include real device imperfections and non-IID signals. Numerical parts are certified and the core argument is formalized.
nodes.status_oct2026: Human progress in 2026: an analytic finite-key proof with source and detector imperfections (arXiv 2606.29943); a numerical framework valid against coherent attacks with non-IID signals (arXiv 2605.12984); a GEO-QKD finite-key feasibility study (arXiv 2605.29706). Entanglement-based passes are finite-key limited (arXiv 2602.11833). Lean-QIT (arXiv 2607.09632) is the first reusable Lean layer for quantum Shannon theory. Catalog: 276 [L] T3; 272 T1.
nodes.premise_tier: T3 (276); T1 (272), conditional for that part
nodes.why: A LEO pass gives a few minutes of link; Jinan-1 shared up to 1.07 Mbit of secure key per pass (Nature, Mar 2025). At such block sizes finite-key penalties are large, and evaluators do not accept proofs that ignore device flaws. Tighter proofs that include imperfections raise certified key per pass (judgment: 10-40% at short passes). More important, they are what a security evaluation needs. The math is hard but within research-grade applied math. Formalization waits on quantum-information coverage in Lean, which S2 assumes catches up during 2027-29.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Key yield is set by loss, background light, weather and detectors, so proof tightness adds tens of percent at most. Satellite QKD as flown uses trusted nodes, so the satellite stays a point of trust whatever the proof says.
nodes.signpost: Eagle-1, SpeQtre or QEYSSat publishing security analyses with machine-checked components; an ETSI or ISO QKD evaluation citing formal proofs.

nodes.title: Certified availability for optical ground networks
nodes.description: Validated stochastic models of cloud, turbulence and pointing outage that predict the availability of a whole optical ground network with site diversity, with bounds good enough to sign service-level agreements against.
nodes.status_oct2026: The bottleneck has moved from peak rate to repeatable service (Turyshev, arXiv 2606.23711, Jun 2026). NASA LCRD two-site combinations gave 83.8-88.5% availability; high reliability may need about 10 sites at least 500 km apart; fixed cost is of order $3-4k per TB at 0.5 h/day of contact. Peak demonstrations: 200 Gbps from LEO (TBIRD), 1.8 Gbps operational GEO relay (EDRS), 267 Mbps from about 19 million miles (DSOC, which ended Sep 2 2025 after returning 13.6 Tbit).
nodes.why: Availability is a correlated-weather problem. Long cloud climatologies exist, so the modeling is cognitive work that compresses under S2. Validation needs multi-year availability records from operating optical networks, which only accumulate in real time; that data gate holds S3 to the S2 year.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Availability is bounded by climatology, and site selection already uses standard cloud statistics, so better models move siting by a few percent. The number of telescopes, a capital decision, sets availability.
nodes.signpost: ESA, NASA, KSAT or a commercial optical network publishing measured multi-site availability against predictions.

nodes.title: Receivers that beat photon counting
nodes.description: Theory and practical designs for joint-detection optical receivers that recover part of the gap between pulse-position modulation with photon counting and the Holevo limit, at deep-space photon flux and realistic background light.
nodes.status_oct2026: The Green Machine receiver showed superadditive capacity over any symbol-by-symbol receiver with BPSK in the photon-starved regime (Nature Communications, 2025). Photon-information-efficiency limits for PPM are reviewed in arXiv 2503.13161; a greedy receiver approaches the Helstrom bound for PPM (arXiv 2403.02634). DSOC used PPM with a 64-pixel superconducting-nanowire detector array (76% detection efficiency) at Palomar. Single-user Holevo capacity of the lossy channel is already known (general), so this node does not depend on family 273.
nodes.why: In the photon-starved regime, each extra bit per received photon is worth as much as a larger ground aperture, and aperture is the dominant cost of a deep-space optical ground terminal. Designing structured quantum measurements with provable gains is theory work that compresses under S2 (cap-physics-theory by 2028-29). Proving that the gain survives background light, loss and timing jitter needs laboratory experiments.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Joint-detection gains shrink quickly with background light and receiver optical loss, and daytime and near-Sun links are background limited. PPM with superconducting detectors is already within a few dB of practical limits (general), and no deep-space optical mission committed before 2031 is known to plan for such a receiver (general).
nodes.signpost: A lab demonstration of a receiver beating optimized PPM photon counting at deep-space-like flux with background; NASA or ESA funding a flight receiver study.

nodes.title: Constellation design with proven compliance
nodes.description: Design tools that co-optimize orbital shells, beam plans, spectrum use and laser topology, and output both a filing-ready design and certified interference and capacity bounds.
nodes.status_oct2026: More than 10,000 commercial communications satellites operate in LEO and 50,000+ more are planned; Amazon filed for a 5,105-satellite direct-to-cell constellation in Jul 2026 (Roberts). On Sep 30 2026 the FCC opened more than 1,000 MHz for satellite services in the 12.7-13.25 GHz and 42-42.5 GHz bands (33FG). Design tools are in-house and uncertified.
nodes.why: As filings multiply and sharing becomes performance-based, value moves to designs that are provably compliant and dense. That needs multiphysics design optimization with guarantees (cap-design-optimization, S2 2028-29) plus the two certified-bound nodes, so it trails them by about a year.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Constellation design is constrained by launch, manufacturing, spectrum rights and business plans. Filings are partly strategic placeholders, and incumbents' in-house tools are good.
nodes.signpost: A filing whose technical annex comes from a design optimizer with certified bounds; a tool vendor or new entrant shipping such a tool.

nodes.title: Tasking and ground planning built on proven limits
nodes.description: Tools for Earth-observation tasking, downlink scheduling, ground-station-as-a-service allocation and ground-station siting that combine exact solvers on structured instances, certified-gap heuristics and documented approximation ceilings, with AI formulating each mission's variant on request.
nodes.status_oct2026: EOS-Bench (arXiv 2604.25782) spans up to 1,000 satellites and 10,000 requests. Exact integer programming for ground-station selection stops scaling before Planet's 96-satellite fleet, while decomposition stays within 95% of optimum on small cases (arXiv 2510.03438). Ground-station-as-a-service revenue scheduling is NP-hard (arXiv 2608.22222). Catalog: 102 [L] T3; 124, 110, 111 and the 125 algorithm T1; 104 [L] T3 only for a randomized version (the deterministic headline and the stochastic and parity extensions are T1).
nodes.why: The ceiling effect is immediate, but most value comes from capability transfer. Each mission has its own constraints (agility, memory, energy, cloud forecasts, contact windows), and a model that formulates and proves a bespoke scheduler in hours replaces months of operations-research work. 124 (conditional) solves exactly the Garey-Johnson three-machine case: unit jobs with precedence constraints on three identical machines, such as three identical antennas or processors with dependency chains. 110 and 111 give worst-case guarantees for online request handling.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Tasking is limited by satellites, agility, cloud cover and downlink, which are physics and capital. The 1+2/e k-median algorithm needs candidate sites and does no better than MIP on siting problems with a few hundred candidates. 111 asserts no polynomial-time implementation, and 124 is a narrow special case.
nodes.signpost: Earth-observation operators or ground-station-as-a-service providers reporting AI-formulated schedulers with certified gaps; public benchmarks reporting optimality gaps alongside scores.

nodes.title: Crypto-agile satellites with proven update paths
nodes.description: Spacecraft security designs that can change algorithms in orbit: hybrid classical plus post-quantum key exchange, hash-based signatures for commands and software, and a code-based fallback such as HQC. Key-management, rekey and update protocols are proven secure by machine and sized for constrained links.
nodes.status_oct2026: NIST IR 8547 (draft, Nov 2024): RSA, ECDSA and ECDH at 112-bit security deprecated by 2030; all quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms disallowed by 2035. NSA CNSA 2.0 sets national-security-system milestones running to 2035 (general). Post-quantum certificate-based authentication is costly on satellite links, which motivates pre-shared-key designs (arXiv 2607.23007) and quantum-safe IKE variants (arXiv 2605.28660). Gidney (arXiv 2505.15917, May 2025) cut the estimate for factoring RSA-2048 to under a million noisy qubits in under a week, from 20 million in 2019.
nodes.why: A GEO satellite launched in 2028 operates to about 2043: eight years past NIST's 2035 cutoff and possibly past the first code-breaking quantum computer. An in-orbit swap path is the only hedge, and it must work the first time. Proving the update and rekey protocols is proof labor that agents remove, and AI cryptanalysis (comms-ai-cryptanalysis) makes the threat model concrete. The band is capped at Medium because government programs need certification acceptance of the evidence.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Migration is mandated regardless of AI. Many satellites use pre-shared symmetric keys (AES-256) for telecommand, which are already quantum-safe, and certification bodies do not yet credit AI-produced proofs.
nodes.signpost: A CCSDS space-link-security profile with hybrid or post-quantum options; a GEO operator announcing in-orbit-updatable post-quantum crypto; NSA or NIAP accepting machine-checked protocol proofs as evidence.

nodes.title: Flight demo of verified post-quantum command links
nodes.description: A satellite flies post-quantum or hybrid authenticated telecommand and key exchange using machine-checked implementations, and performs an in-orbit algorithm swap.
nodes.status_oct2026: We found no flight with machine-checked implementations. Several firms have announced post-quantum crypto demonstrations on small satellites since 2025 (general, unverified).
nodes.why: Once the architecture and verified code exist, a demo needs only a rideshare slot and a cooperative bus. Launch cadence does not bind for a cubesat-class demo, but integration lead times of 12-18 months do (general). The in-orbit swap is the new part: it shows the 15-year-asset problem can be managed.
nodes.strongest_case_small: This adds assurance, not capability. Post-quantum crypto can fly without proofs, and the first operators to need it (governments) will use their own certified modules.
nodes.signpost: An announced mission plan with an in-orbit post-quantum algorithm swap and published proofs.

nodes.title: Ground demo: optical receiver beats photon counting
nodes.description: A ground or lab demonstration in which a joint-detection receiver beats optimized PPM with photon counting by 25% or more in bits per received photon, at deep-space-like photon flux and background.
nodes.status_oct2026: Superadditivity has been shown in the lab with BPSK (Green Machine, 2025), but not under deep-space conditions with background light.
nodes.why: Even with designs in hand by 2029 (S2), building low-loss photonic circuits and testing them against realistic background takes a year or more. S3's autonomous labs shorten the iteration loop but not fabrication.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Gains shrink with background light and optical loss, the PPM-plus-SNSPD baseline keeps improving, and there is no flight slot to use such a receiver before 2031.
nodes.signpost: A peer-reviewed demonstration at photon flux and background matching a Mars-distance link.

nodes.title: Multi-node satellite QKD demonstrations
nodes.description: Satellite QKD missions deliver keys among three or more ground nodes in different countries in routine campaigns: Eagle-1 in-orbit validation, SpeQtre, QEYSSat, SPOQC and successors to China's Jinan-1.
nodes.status_oct2026: Jinan-1 (Nature, Mar 19 2025): 23 kg payload, ~100 kg portable ground station, up to 1.07 Mbit of secure key per pass, and a key between China and South Africa over 12,900 km (trusted-node satellite). ESA lists Eagle-1's launch for late 2026/early 2027, followed by three years of in-orbit validation. The SpeQtre ground campaign produced 7.56 kbps at 4.78% QBER over 1.8 km (arXiv 2605.19689). QEYSSat has a digital twin (arXiv 2608.21968), and the SPOQC continuous-variable QKD cubesat was planned for early 2026 (arXiv 2602.23510).
nodes.why: These missions are funded and largely built, so they run on the physical clock regardless of AI mathematics. They are the platform where AI-tightened proofs (comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs) would be applied.
nodes.strongest_case_small: This node is the physical anchor: no scenario moves it, and AI mathematics adds little to it.
nodes.signpost: Eagle-1 launch and its first published key-exchange campaign.

nodes.title: Mega-constellation mesh run with certified optimality
nodes.description: A large LEO operator runs laser-mesh routing and radio resource allocation in production with certified per-snapshot optimality gaps and verified control-plane software.
nodes.status_oct2026: No operator has disclosed this. Starlink, Amazon Leo and SDA's transport layer (21 Tranche 1 satellites launched Sep 2025, per 33FG) run proprietary or government software stacks.
nodes.why: Software rolls out at the speed of an operator's deployment pipeline, so this node tracks its cognitive prerequisites closely. Value: judgment of 5-20% more delivered capacity at fixed hardware, plus fewer control-plane outages. Mega-constellation revenues are tens of billions of dollars a year (general), so even 5% is a lot of money, which is why adoption is likely once the tools exist.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Operators may already be near-optimal on their own instances. Hardware upgrades (V3: 10x per satellite) and the regulatory lift (EPFD reform, reported at up to 7x capacity) dwarf a software gain (33FG), and certificates are a nice-to-have.
nodes.signpost: Operator engineering talks or filings citing optimality gaps or formal verification of routing; SDA contract language requiring them.

nodes.title: Predictive coexistence scheduling for direct-to-device
nodes.description: Direct-to-device and broadband constellations schedule beams, power and emissions against certified interference budgets for adjacent bands, other operators and radio astronomy, instead of using blunt avoidance zones.
nodes.status_oct2026: SkyShare (arXiv 2609.00821) schedules spot beams within EPFD-budgeted regions and cuts unserved cells by up to 90.68% versus boresight avoidance at 25 radio-astronomy sites, using Starlink geometry. The 2620 MHz D2D downlink's second harmonic already causes at least 59% geodetic-VLBI data loss (arXiv 2608.11659). D2D spectrum is consolidating: in May 2026 the FCC approved EchoStar's spectrum sale to SpaceX with a $2.4B escrow, and Starlink's D2C service got a +10 dB power waiver in Mar 2025 (33FG).
nodes.why: Coexistence is moving from static masks to dynamic, budgeted scheduling, and doing it precisely gains operators served cells, so incentives line up. Certified budgets let science users and regulators trust a schedule without seeing proprietary traffic.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Harmonics and out-of-band emissions are fixed by filters in hardware, not by scheduling. D2D capacity is set by spectrum holdings, aperture size and power, and operators have weak incentives to protect science bands without regulation.
nodes.signpost: An operator agreement with a radio observatory or NSF that uses predictive, budgeted scheduling; an FCC order referencing certified coexistence budgets.

nodes.title: Weather-robust optical ground network service
nodes.description: An optical ground network sells weather-inclusive availability of about 99% for LEO or GEO data return, using site diversity, availability models and autonomous scheduling.
nodes.status_oct2026: Operational optical relay exists: EDRS at 1.8 Gbps, with 80,000+ links at 99.53% reliability (arXiv 2606.23711). Direct-to-ground optical service at high availability does not yet exist at scale.
nodes.why: Better models and schedulers say where to put telescopes and how to use them. The telescopes, sites, fiber and staff are capital that no scenario makes free. S2 moves the date by removing the planning delay, not the build.
nodes.strongest_case_small: RF ground networks already deliver, and demand for optical downlink may stay limited to a few high-rate customers. Capital cycles for ground networks are long.
nodes.signpost: A commercial optical ground network announcing an availability service-level agreement; ESA or NASA contracting for optical ground service at a stated availability.

nodes.title: Certified operational space QKD service
nodes.description: A sovereign satellite QKD service routinely delivers keys to government users across 10 or more ground nodes, with a security evaluation that accepts its finite-key proof (for example EuroQCI's space segment).
nodes.status_oct2026: Demonstrations only (see comms-space-qkd-network-demo). China is likely to field an operational quantum-communication constellation first, on its own timeline (general, unverified).
nodes.why: The service needs satellites, ground terminals and a security evaluation; AI mathematics shortens only the evaluation. The band is capped at Medium because it needs certification acceptance. The physical clock (procurement, launch) sets the year, which is why S3 equals S2.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Western security agencies have preferred post-quantum cryptography to QKD for national-security use (general). Trusted-node satellites limit the security gain, and budgets may go to PQC instead.
nodes.signpost: A EuroQCI space-segment procurement award; an accredited security evaluation of a satellite QKD service.

nodes.title: Satellite fleets crypto-agile before the 2035 cutoff
nodes.description: From this year, most new government and major commercial satellites carry in-orbit-updatable post-quantum crypto with machine-checked update paths, and legacy fleets are protected by ground-side controls.
nodes.status_oct2026: Government migration planning is under way (NIST IR 8547, CNSA 2.0); space-specific post-quantum profiles are still being written (general).
nodes.why: Mandates drive the migration; AI mathematics makes the verified version affordable. Procurement cycles (contracts signed 2-4 years before launch) set the pace, which is why S3 does not beat S2.
nodes.strongest_case_small: The migration happens with or without AI proofs. The AI contribution is assurance quality, which buyers may not pay for.
nodes.signpost: Government satellite RFPs requiring crypto-agility and machine-checked evidence; the first GEO comsat contract with in-orbit post-quantum update.

nodes.title: Software's share of constellation capacity gains
nodes.description: AI-produced mathematics and software (certified optimization, coexistence scheduling, custom codes, design tools) account for at least 10% of a major constellation's gain in usable capacity per satellite between 2026 and 2031.
nodes.status_oct2026: Capacity gains for 2026-2031 are dominated by hardware (V3 satellites: a 10x per-satellite step) and regulation (EPFD reform; Ku co-frequency beams per location from 1 to 8) (33FG).
nodes.why: If hardware gives 10x and software 10-30% on top, software's share of the multiplied gain is small, but at mega-constellation scale it can be billions of dollars a year (judgment). Under S2 the software nodes land in 2028-29, so the effect is visible by 2030.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Attribution is nearly impossible from outside and operators will not disclose it; hardware and spectrum dominate.
nodes.signpost: Operator statements attributing capacity gains to software or AI; capacity per satellite rising faster than hardware specifications imply.

nodes.title: Machine-checked crypto becomes a procurement norm
nodes.description: Government space buyers (for example SDA, or ESA for IRIS²) require machine-checked implementation and protocol proofs for the security functions of new satellites.
nodes.status_oct2026: We found no such requirement. Aviation already gives credit for formal methods (DO-333) (general), but AI-produced proofs are not qualified tools today (tl-position-6).
nodes.why: Once proofs are cheap and have been shown in flight, buyers can demand them at little cost; this is the strategic payoff of the verification channel. The band is capped at Medium because it needs tool qualification and regulator acceptance.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Procurement rules change slowly and are written by people who distrust AI-generated evidence. Tool qualification may lag well past 2031.
nodes.signpost: An SDA, ESA or NSA solicitation listing machine-checked proofs as a requirement or evaluation credit.

nodes.title: International shift to provable spectrum sharing
nodes.description: The ITU follows the FCC in replacing fixed EPFD limits with performance-based sharing criteria and checkable compliance showings.
nodes.status_oct2026: The FCC moved domestically on Apr 30 2026 (33FG). ITU Radio Regulations Article 22 EPFD limits remain, and changing them needs a decision at a World Radiocommunication Conference: WRC-27 in late 2027, the next around 2031 (general).
nodes.why: Certified showings remove one technical objection to performance-based rules (that compliance cannot be checked). The decision itself is political and runs on a four-year conference cycle that needs consensus among administrations, many of them protective of GSO incumbents. No scenario moves the calendar.
nodes.strongest_case_small: GSO operators and many administrations oppose relaxing the limits, and the issue may not be on an agenda before the conference around 2031.
nodes.signpost: The WRC-27 outcome on Article 22 and the agenda set for the following conference; ITU-R study groups adopting performance-based methods.

nodes.title: Code-breaking quantum computer before 2031
nodes.description: A quantum computer able to break RSA-2048 or 256-bit elliptic-curve keys exists before the end of 2031. It would expose legacy satellite links and any recorded traffic protected by them.
nodes.status_oct2026: Gidney (May 2025): RSA-2048 needs under a million noisy qubits running for under a week. Family 279 (exact quantum factoring over a fixed gate set, T1) makes Shor's algorithm succeed with probability one in theory but does not reduce qubit or error-correction budgets (tl-position-5). The largest systems remain far below that scale (general).
nodes.why: This is a hardware race. Under S3, AI that speeds up its own hardware and runs closed-loop experiments could also compress quantum-hardware design loops; that is the only route by which the world of this release raises the risk. Fabrication, yield and cryogenics still bind. It matters here because any satellite whose key exchange is RSA or ECC, and whose traffic was recorded, is exposed when this node fires, which is why the crypto-agility nodes matter now.
nodes.strongest_case_small: Scaling from today's hundreds to thousands of physical qubits to about a million error-corrected qubits in five years is far beyond historical trends, and most expert surveys put it later (general).
nodes.signpost: Logical-qubit demonstrations at scale with error rates below threshold; new resource estimates below 100,000 noisy qubits for RSA-2048.

scenario_contrast: S1 (plateau, analyst default): the research-grade model stays internal until about 2027-28. Communications gets the fast items first: proven ceilings for partitioning, siting and scheduling (102 at T3, others conditional) take effect in 2027 once someone runs Comparator, and AI cryptanalysis audits of non-standard protocols are already happening. Verified post-quantum code for space processors arrives around 2028, certified network optimization around 2028, certified interference showings and verified control-plane software around 2029-30. Nothing physical moves early. S2 (exponential, base case): with task horizons doubling every 6-9 months and public access within 6-12 months, every cognitive node in this tree moves 1-2 years earlier. Certified mesh optimization, verified PQC and code design arrive in 2027; certified interference bounds, verified routing and finite-key QKD proofs in 2028; design optimizers and receiver theory in 2029. Operators can adopt software nodes almost immediately, so tier-6 software outcomes (certified mesh operations in 2028, coexistence scheduling in 2029) follow closely. Physical and institutional gates do not compress: launch and integration lead times, telescope and ground-station capital, spectrum rights and the ITU conference calendar (no international sharing change before about 2031), security certification and procurement cycles (crypto-agile fleets about 2029-30 in both S1 and S2), and the QKD satellites already being built (multi-node demos 2028 in every scenario). S3 (recursive): cognition is near-free from 2028, so design tools and receiver theory land a year earlier still, but tier-5 to tier-7 nodes move by at most a year. The one place S3 changes the risk picture is cryptography, in both directions: cheaper cryptanalysis raises the small chance of a lattice weakness being found (Low rather than Speculative), and AI-accelerated quantum hardware design raises the chance of a code-breaking quantum computer before 2031 from Speculative to Low. Across scenarios the gap between cognitive and physical clocks widens: by 2029 under S2, the math for denser, provably compliant, provably secure constellations will be ahead of the satellites, spectrum rules and certifiers that would use it.
key_insights: The math communications actually spends effort on is bespoke and expert-scarce, not famous: interference statistics, routing and resource-allocation optimization, scheduling, short-block coding, and protocol and crypto verification. The catalog touches it mainly through ceilings (UGC, sparsest cut, k-median) and through quantum and optical capacity theorems that confirm what engineers already assumed (tl-position-4, fc-position-2).

Regulators just turned spectrum compliance into a math problem. The FCC's 2026 move from fixed EPFD masks to performance-based criteria (3% throughput degradation, 0.1-0.4% added unavailability, judged by simulation) makes certified interference bounds the highest-leverage communications application of AI mathematics. Their adoption is limited by operators and regulators accepting them, not by the math.

Because joint laser-terminal pairing, routing and rate allocation is NP-hard per snapshot, the deliverable is a certificate (a proven optimality gap), not an optimum. Certificates convert 'should we buy more lasers or write better software?' into a measured number. Realistic gains over operators' current practice are probably 5-20% capacity (judgment), small next to the 10x V3 hardware step and the regulatory lift.

Nothing in the release weakens deployed or post-quantum cryptography: 279 does not reduce qubit budgets, and 138 does not touch lattices. The risk is the capability. AI agents already broke eight non-standard published constructions in Aug 2026. For satellites launched from 2027 that will operate into the 2040s, the right response is crypto-agility with machine-checked update paths, which is itself something AI makes cheap.

Statement gaps matter even in the 'solid' families. For 117 the Lean main result is the SDP integrality gap, not the NP-hardness headline. For 125 Lean covers a companion recovery result, not the 1+2/e algorithm. For 104 Lean covers a randomized version. Planners should treat those headlines as T1 until audited.

Optical and quantum link performance through 2031 is set by apertures, detectors, weather, pass geometry and launches. Capacity theorems (273 conditional, 276) change confidence, not data rates. The genuinely open, AI-relevant optical problem is receivers that beat photon counting, and its first payoff is a ground demo around 2030 under S2.

Under S2 the cognitive nodes move 1-2 years earlier and software-only outcomes follow within a year, but every node gated by launch, capital, spectrum rights, the ITU calendar or certification moves by a year at most. The exponential shows up as a growing gap between what can be proven and what can be flown, licensed or certified.

Fastest effects (2027 in all scenarios): proven ceilings for tasking and partitioning (P3), and AI audits of bespoke satellite security protocols (P1->P3). Slowest: an international spectrum regime change and certified operational QKD service, neither plausible before about 2030-31 in any scenario.
nil_effects: Deployed cryptography (AES, RSA, ECC, ML-KEM, ML-DSA) is unaffected by the catalog. 279 makes Shor's algorithm exact in theory but does not cut qubit or error-correction budgets, and 138 (Subset Sum in 2^0.49n worst case) is irrelevant to lattice parameters (tl-position-5).

The release's galactic speedups (FFT below n log n, matrix-multiplication exponent ≤ 9/4) give no onboard signal-processing or beamforming speedup (tl-position-1); 120's almost-linear matching is irrelevant at constellation scale, where classical matching already runs in milliseconds.

Link budgets and data rates do not change through 2031 because of any theorem. Optical rates are set by aperture, detector efficiency, pointing and weather; D2D rates by spectrum holdings, satellite aperture and power; deep-space optical by terminals already built (DSOC ended Sep 2025).
Spectrum allocations and the ITU conference calendar: no amount of cognition moves WRC decisions, and international EPFD limits stay in force at least until the conference after WRC-27 (general).
Satellite QKD key rates and coverage are set by loss, background light, clouds and pass duration. 266, 272 and 276 change no protocol on Eagle-1, SpeQtre, QEYSSat or Jinan-class payloads.
Number of laser terminals per satellite, acquisition times and launch cadence, which set mesh capacity more than routing software does.
Quantum optimization for satellite scheduling: 281 (QAOA reaches the SK optimum when size goes to infinity before depth) does not imply any near-term quantum advantage for tasking or routing.
The 2030 and 2035 post-quantum migration deadlines are set by NIST and NSA, not by AI mathematics. AI changes the cost of doing the migration verifiably, not its date.

signposts.event: First independent Comparator run and statement audit on any openai/math communications-relevant challenge (UniqueGamesTheorem.json, AmplitudeDamping.json, UniformSparsestCut.json, KMedianRecovery.json).
signposts.what_it_changes: Moves the ceilings and the 276 capacity result from T3 to T4; confirms the P3 nodes for 2027 and lets planners cite the theorems without caveat. A failed audit would downgrade comms-hardness-ceilings-settled and everything that relies on it.

signposts.event: A research-grade math model becomes available to outside engineering teams at a usable price (any lab).
signposts.what_it_changes: Starts the P1 clock for comms-certified-network-optimization, comms-code-design-on-demand and comms-hardness-aware-tasking. Before mid-2027 it confirms S2 timing; slipping past 2028 confirms S1.

signposts.event: An FCC filing, ITU-R WP4A contribution or bilateral coordination agreement that cites machine-checked or interval-certified interference bounds.
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms comms-certified-interference-bounds and pulls the D2D coexistence and constellation-design nodes forward a year. Absence through 2028 under public model access would point to regulatory culture, not math, as the gate.

signposts.event: An AI-produced cryptanalysis result against a NIST-standardized scheme or its parameters (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, HQC), or expert confirmation or refutation of the Luo ML-KEM quantum-attack claim (arXiv 2605.17412).
signposts.what_it_changes: A confirmed result moves comms-lattice-weakness from watch item to active and makes crypto-agility an urgent retrofit for satellites in build. A refutation leaves the bands as stated.

signposts.event: Eagle-1 launch and first key-exchange campaign, plus any published security analysis with machine-checked components.
signposts.what_it_changes: Anchors the physical QKD timeline (comms-space-qkd-network-demo, 2028) and tests whether formal finite-key proofs become part of space QKD evaluation (comms-finite-key-qkd-proofs).

signposts.event: A verified PQC library for a radiation-hardened processor or space FPGA, or a CCSDS space-link-security profile with hybrid or post-quantum options.
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms comms-pq-verified-implementations and starts the clock on crypto-agile architectures and the verified-command-link flight demo.

signposts.event: A mega-constellation operator or SDA disclosing optimality-gap metrics or formal verification of routing or handover software.
signposts.what_it_changes: Confirms comms-certified-mesh-operations and gives the first observable data on how much capacity software leaves on the table versus hardware.

signposts.event: Quantum-hardware milestones: logical qubits at scale below threshold, or a published RSA-2048 resource estimate under 100,000 noisy qubits.
signposts.what_it_changes: Raises comms-crqc-before-2031 and the urgency of PQ migration for legacy fleets, independently of AI mathematics.
